labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Seen on 2026-11-12, a day with about 50 merges: `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one integer that every process PR increments in its own branch. Each time one of them merges, every other open process PR either conflicts on that one line (GitHub shows CONFLICTING and the PR drops out of a merge run) or, worse, carries the SAME new number and merges cleanly - two process changes then share one number and a fork that already synced at it never pulls the second (it happened with #1117 and #930 at 17; fixed by the extra bump PR #1142). Today #965, #967, #972, #1033, #1024, #1100, #1116 and #1151 all had to be renumbered by hand, some more than once.

The law today (AGENTS.md "Process changes bump PROCESS_VERSION"): the PR increments the number; "whichever merges second takes the next number when it merges main".

Proposal to decide (maintainer): the number is not written in the PR at all. A process PR only says in its body "process change: yes" (the reviewer checks that instead of the bump); the merging session increments `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` right after the merge in a one-line follow-up PR (or the merge tooling does: `cargo xtask process-bump`), and posts the #681 announcement with that number. One writer, no conflicts, no shared numbers. Alternatives: derive the version from the count of merge commits touching the process paths (no file at all), or keep the file and make `.gitattributes` resolve it with a custom "max + 1" merge driver (needs local git config on every clone, so probably not).

Done means: the chosen rule is in AGENTS.md (and the review-prs / merge-ready skills), two process PRs open at once no longer conflict with each other, and two of them can never land on the same number; `PROCESS_VERSION` bumped and announced for this change itself.

title: Verifier crossing law (a) is exact-sign: a shared end a rounding apart can hold the post

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7

body:
Found while fixing #1048.

The verifier's crossing law (a) (`crates/sim/src/verify/laws.rs`, `proper_cross`, asked by `verify/crossing.rs` of every Feed-Feed chord pair of different moves at a shared depth) tests exact signs: an orientation of exactly 0 is a touch, anything else counts. Two moves that meet at one vertex reached twice, a rounding apart (an orbit closing a ulp off its start, a microlift return landing on a chord end, a ring starting on the last ring's vertex), can therefore read as a proper crossing. `Warning::Crossing` blocks the post.

The #1048 fix widens the adaptive planner's own check (`motion/.../adaptive/guard.rs`, `crosses`) to read "on the other chord's line" within `TOUCH` = 1e-9 mm. The planner now accepts such a plan where it used to fall back to Offset rings, but the verifier still uses the exact zero. If the posted moves keep a rounding-apart shared vertex, the post is held by a Crossing warning instead. That is still safe (refused by name), but the two laws should agree: the plan check is meant to be the verifier's law asked first.

Expected: law (a) reads a chord end within the same stated tolerance of the other chord's line as on it (sign 0), so its verdict matches the planner's `guard::crosses`. A real crossing still blocks. Under the safety floor (a verifier law), with a pin pair: a shared vertex 1e-12 mm apart does not warn, and a crossing a micron through still does.

Done means: a `crates/sim` verify test where two Feed moves share an end 1e-12 mm apart gives no Crossing warning; a micron crossing still does; the crossing suites and the bucketed-vs-all-pairs reference stay green.

Related: #1048, #980, #1010.

body:
Found by the high-tier review of PR #1097 (review comment on that PR, head 56e30159); older than that PR.

**What.** The GUI clears the world before it opens a project. The MCP tool `open_project` and the script verb `cam.load` do not: they load the file into the live world, so state of the previous document that the file does not overwrite stays behind. The reviewer's probe: document A carried a per-setup mark on a model named "casting"; after `open_project` of document B, A's mark was still there and applied to B's model of the same name. In that probe the gate still refused (B's operations read as stale), so no wrong program was posted - but nothing guarantees that for other leftovers (setups, fixtures, tools, undo history, cached toolpaths or verdicts of entities whose names collide).

**Why P1.** An agent driving CamCraft headlessly gets a document that is a mix of two files, without a word. If a concrete case is found where a leftover changes a posted program or passes a gate, re-rate it P0.

**Expected.** Opening a project is the same operation on every surface: the previous document is cleared (and the undo history with it) before the file is applied, through one shared app-layer path the GUI, MCP, script and CLI all call. If the MCP session has unsaved changes, the tool says so in its reply (or refuses unless told to discard - decide and record).

Done means: `open_project` / `cam.load` after another document leave nothing of the first one (entities, components, history, caches), pinned by a test that opens A then B headlessly and compares the world with B opened fresh; the GUI path uses the same function.

body:
Part of #290. Found while working #532 (Wire EDM: 2-axis contour op).

**What happens:** the Wire Contour operation (#532) is created and edited through the same undoable commands as every other kind (`CreateOperation`, `EditOperationParams`), and its parameters already ride the JSON door the MCP uses (`project::params_to_json` / `params_from_json`: `wire_contour { top_z, bottom_z, condition, side, start }`). But an agent cannot make one over MCP today:

- `add_operation` requires a non-empty `"tool"` (`mcp::tools::req_str`, and `"tool"` is in the schema's `required` list). A Wire Contour mounts no library tool - the wire is the machine's EDM condition (#531) - and `CreateOperation` refuses one that names a tool.
- No MCP tool mounts a machine file that states `edm.conditions`. The EDM templates are test fixtures, not library machines, until the wire post lands (#530's decision, #533), so a headless session has no wire EDM to create the op on.
- `list_operation_types` lists the kind with an empty `tool_kinds` and nothing that says "pass no tool"; the camcraft-mcp skill does not mention the kind.

**Expected:** `add_operation` with `kind: "Wire Contour"` and no `tool` (or an empty one), plus `params: { condition, side, start }`, creates the op on a setup that mounts a wire EDM; `edit_operation` patches `side`, `start` and `condition`; the refusals arrive as tool errors with the command's own words (no condition named, a condition with no gap or no wire diameter, a tool named on a wire cut).

**Scope:**
- `add_operation`: `tool` optional for a kind whose `KindInfo::mounts_tool()` is false; the schema's `required` and the description say so.

body:
Noted by the high-tier review of PR #1082 (review comment on that PR, head 642cd694); true on main before that PR as well, so not a regression of it.

**What.** The index-swing check (#804 / #810 / #818, `crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs`) judges the tool against the work as the rotary indexes. It does not judge the swept WORK (part, stock, and what turns with them) against what stands still under it: the machine table, a fixture plate, a rotary subplate. A long or wide workpiece on a low rotary can swing into the table or plate during an index and the program posts.

Related gap from the same review: a rotary standing directly on a fixture plate with no subplate is judged on the bare-table figure ("a plate alone raises nothing", by design) with no named note.

**Why P1, not P0, for now.** It is a collision the check does not look for, not one it looks for and gets wrong, and it is unknown how much of the table/plate geometry the check can read today (the machine file states `nose_to_axis`; the table's extent may not be stated at all). If the first step shows the figures are there and a real setup passes, re-rate it P0.

Done means: it is stated (decision file) what the swing check judges and against which bodies; the swept work's largest radius about the rotary line is judged against the stated distance from the centerline to the table / plate / subplate top, with a refusal by name when it does not clear and a named "not judged" note when the machine states no figure to judge it against; pinned by tests with a workpiece that clears and one that does not.

title: Add built-in vise: "Fit to the stock" fails with "invalid parameters: setup 'Setup1' has no stock" and the dialog never says the stock must be set first

labels.name: bug

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat (2026-11-12, v0.18.0, with a screenshot), filed by an agent for him: "it is unclear how the built-in vise are supposed to work, and we cannot figure it out, we just get an error on fit to the stock".

**What he did.** New document, one setup (`Setup1`, active), a model imported (`Milling-test`), no stock defined yet (the browser still shows a `Stock` node under the setup). Fixtures -> Add built-in vise... -> picked "125 mm self-centering" -> left "Fit to the stock (centred, jaws closed on it)" ticked (the default) -> Place.

**What happens.** Nothing is placed. The dialog, the Fixtures page and the status bar all show, in red: `vise not placed: invalid parameters: setup 'Setup1' has no stock to fit the vise to`.

**Why.** `InsertVise::new` (`crates/app/src/commands/builtin_vise.rs`) with `VisePlacement::FitStock` reads `model::stock_world_aabb_for`, which is `None` while the setup's stock entity has no body. The refusal is right - there is nothing to fit to - but:
1. The dialog offers "Fit to the stock" ticked by default when the setup has no stock, and only says so after Place.
2. The message does not say what to do: set the stock first (Stock page), or untick the box and place the vise by position.
3. "invalid parameters:" is our word, not the user's; nothing he typed was invalid.
4. The dialog does not say how a built-in vise works at all: where it lands when fitted (fixed jaw against the stock's +Y side, centred in X, jaw floor under the stock, opening = the stock's Y width; a self-centering one centred in X and Y), what the figures mean for the fit, and that the placed vise is then judged in the collision checks.
5. The browser shows a `Stock` node for a setup whose stock has no body, so "has no stock" reads as wrong.

**Wanted**
- When the active setup has no stock body: the dialog says so before Place, in plain English ("This setup has no stock yet. Set the stock (Stock page) to fit the vise to it, or place the vise by position below."), with a button that opens the Stock page; "Fit to the stock" is off and greyed with that reason, and the position rows show.
- With a stock: one or two plain lines under the checkbox saying where the vise will land and how far the jaws open, from the stock's real figures (e.g. "Opens to 80.0 mm on the stock's Y width; stock sits on the jaw floor"), and a named refusal up front when the stock is wider than the vise's max opening.
- Refusal texts on this path lose the "invalid parameters:" prefix and say what to do next.
- The same for the two siblings that fail the same way: "Add mod vise pair" (`commands/mod_vise.rs`, "has no stock to fit the mod vise to") and parallels under the stock (`commands/accessory.rs`, "has no stock to fit the parallels under").
- A stock that has no body yet is shown as such in the browser (e.g. `Stock  not set`), the way `Machine  no machine` is.

Not wanted here: fitting the vise to the part instead of the stock, or creating a stock automatically - a vise holds the stock; if a default stock at import is wanted, that is its own issue.

Done means: on a setup without stock the dialog explains and offers the Stock page before any Place, and Place by position works; with a stock, Fit places the vise and the dialog said beforehand where; the three refusals read in plain English; pinned in the structural tests (labels, the greyed checkbox and its reason, the button) and by app tests for the refusal texts. No command semantics change; no snapshot PNG touched.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer, 2026-11-12: "the wasm32 app should be loadable from the github pages for easy access". Filed by an agent for him (no `source:agent`: it is his request).

**Where things stand**
- GitHub Pages is now enabled for this repo (source: GitHub Actions) at https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft/. The `site` and `pages` jobs of `release.yml` build the Zola site in `site/` and deploy it on a release tag (#688). The `github-pages` environment allows `v*.*.0` tags to deploy.
- The wasm32 shell runs in a browser on WebGL2 (#31, PR #847): `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` writes `<target>/web/` with `index.html`, `wasi_shim.js`, `camcraft-ui.js` and `camcraft-ui_bg.wasm`. Nothing publishes that folder; today it only runs from a local http server.
- The site's front page already says the browser build comes "once the app and its interface build for the web".

**What is wanted**
The released wasm32 build is served from the Pages site, so anyone can open CamCraft in a browser from a link, without installing anything.
- The app lives under a fixed path of the site (e.g. `/Camcraft/app/`), with a clear link from the front page and the guide's first-run page.
- It is built in the release workflow from the tagged tree (a job that runs `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` and hands its output to the `site` job, which places it in the Pages artifact) - **no new `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger** (Actions budget). Linux runner; say in the PR how many billed minutes it adds to a cut.
- Everything the page loads resolves under the project sub-path (`/Camcraft/app/...`, not `/`): the import map, `wasi_shim.js`, the `.js`/`.wasm` pair, any asset fetch. A fork's own Pages (another owner or repo name) must work too, as the `site` job's `--base-url` already does.
- The page says what it is: the version it was built from, that it runs in the browser on WebGL2, and what does not work there yet (the list on #31: file picker, playback without threads, WebGPU).
- A failed wasm build must not withhold the docs site or the release: the docs deploy without `/app/` and the run names what failed (the way `publish` treats a failed platform build).

**Known obstacles**
- #949: the build script rewrites the checkout's `Cargo.lock`; in CI that must not leak into anything packaged from the same checkout.
- `.wasm` size and Pages limits (1 GB site, 100 MB per file): state the size in the PR; use `wasm-opt` if it is needed and available without a new unpinned download.
- Pages serves no custom headers (no COOP/COEP), so nothing may depend on `SharedArrayBuffer` / threads.

Done means: after a release tag, `https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft/app/` loads the shell of that release in a current Chrome and Firefox, linked from the site's front page; pinned by a check in the workflow that the Pages artifact holds `app/index.html` and the `.wasm`, and by a test or script check that the page's URLs are relative to its own folder.

Part of #688 (docs and browser build on Pages); builds on #31 (the app and UI on wasm).

body:
Noted by the high-tier review of PR #1043 (review comment on that PR, head 1a6d4017). The law is on main (#369); PR #1043 is what first lets a user reach it.

**What.** `Reach::radii` reads a lathe holder body point at radius `|X + x|`, where `X` is the tool tip's signed radial position and `x` the body point's radial offset in the turning tool frame. The UI and MCP wording says "+x points away from the spindle axis". Both are true only for a tip at X >= 0.

- Facing a little past centre (tip at a small negative X): `X + x` is still the body's real position, so the reading is right; only the wording is loose.
- A tool that really sits on the other side of the axis (a rear turret or gang position programmed at negative X), if any turning path can carry one: the body would be read mirrored through the axis, so a holder that hits could be judged clear.

**Not known.** Whether any turning operation or machine definition today can put a tip at a negative X other than the facing overrun. If none can, this is a wording fix plus a guard; if one can, it is a collision-law defect and should be re-rated P0.

Done means: it is stated (with a test) which signed-X cases the turning generators can produce; the law either handles a tip on the negative side correctly or refuses it by name; the UI/MCP wording says what +x means for both cases.

title: A stock-from-model's source model left in the tree is judged as a part: the program verdict reports a gouge for any cut into the casting

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while reproducing #1091 (and the reason the #1077 reviewer's probe got a second, unrelated refusal).

**What happens.** Import a casting, set the stock to "from model" with that casting as its source, import the part, and machine it. The casting stays in the tree as a model, and `stock_sim::part_facets_as_modelled` reads every non-fixture model as the part. So the program verdict judges the casting as finished geometry, and any cut into it - every cut, since the casting is the stock - is a gouge: `post blocked - gouge: program cuts below the model in 812 cell(s), worst 20.00 mm at (-1.75, -7.75, z 10.00)` (a Bore of a 16 mm hole in a part under a stepped casting, fixture of `crates/app/tests/stepped_stock_rapid.rs` without its `DeleteEntity` of the casting).

**Expected.** A model that is only the source of a `FromModel` stock is stock, not part: the verdict (and the field view) should not read it as finished geometry. (Possibly: a model that is the source of the stock and is not the source of any operation.)

**Workaround in the #1091 tests.** Delete the casting after `SetStock` - the stock keeps its own copy of the facets.

Done means: a casting used as from-model stock and left in the tree posts a legal program over a separate part, pinned by a test; a model that is both the stock source and an op's source (`edge_break_gate.rs`'s brick) keeps today's verdict.

body:
**What:** `solid_law_goldens::every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` (#862, #1000) judges every posted `.nc` golden whose stem has a `.cl` golden. Since #1000 its `UNJUDGED` list holds one entry: `arc_planes`. That program is hand-built in `crates/app/tests/arc_planes.rs` (a G18 and a G19 arc between XY arcs, for the five dialect posts). No operation kind, part, region or tool record makes it, so no gate a user's post runs can judge it. The guard can't tell a synthetic posting fixture from an op program nobody judged, so it keeps a by-name exception list.

**Why it matters:** a by-name exception list is where an unjudged op golden can hide later. A synthetic fixture should say what it is in the golden itself, the way a refused program carries the "refused program, posted for syntax conformance" first line.

**Done means:** posted goldens of hand-built posting fixtures (today `arc_planes` in Fanuc, haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain) carry a first-line marker the guard recognises (e.g. "synthetic program, posted for syntax conformance"), written by the suite's regeneration path (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test arc_planes`) and not by hand. Alternatively the fixture gets a part and a gate that judges it. `UNJUDGED` is then empty and removed, so any new unjudged posted golden fails the guard.

Found by the #1000 worker. Part of #1000's follow-up.

body:
Found by the high-tier review of PR #1077 (review comment on that PR, head c6c658db). Present on main for part-sourced Bores; PR #1077 extends the same reading to stock-sourced Bore and Thread.

**What happens.** Verify's rapid law (#96, `RapidInStock`) caps the stock column at the flat `stock_top_z`, the highest point of the whole stock. On a stock that is not a flat-topped box - a "from model" casting or a carried stock with a boss - a rapid down to just above a lower surface is judged as if the stock stood at its highest point there too.

Reviewer's probe: stock solid to Z 20 over the hole's mouth, with a boss to Z 30 elsewhere. A Bore on that hole (part-sourced and stock-sourced alike) rapids from clearance to Z 22, 2 mm above the real stock under it, and is convicted `RapidInStock { at: 0 }`. The post is blocked for a legal program.

**Expected.** The law reads the stock's top at the rapid's XY (the local column), not the global maximum. A rapid that ends above the stock really under it passes; a rapid into stock that really stands there is still convicted.

**Why P1.** It refuses, it does not gouge - but a user with a casting or a stepped stock cannot post a correct program. The probe also imported the casting as a model, which added a gouge refusal of its own, so the first step is a clean reproduction with stock only.

**Careful.** This is a gouge law: loosening it must not let any rapid into real stock pass. Carried stock, a faced top (`acquit_by_prior`), the 3+2 site and Thread's descent all read the same cap.

Done means: a pinning test with a stepped stock where the dive over the low part passes and the same dive over the boss is convicted, for a part-sourced and a stock-sourced Bore; the existing rapid-law tests (`ladder_entry_height`, the #96 pins) unchanged.

Found while working #1057 (on a full-fidelity model, so not a fidelity bug).

**What happens.** A Thread (thread mill) operation sourced from a model is convicted with `Gouge` on every helix move, and `Crossing` pairs, even at full fidelity. Fixture: `crates/app/tests/coarse_rims.rs` on `issue/1057-drill-excess-false-gouge` (PR for #1057) - the 40 x 40 x 20 block with a 20 x 20 cavity blind at Z 10, a 6 mm Tap-form thread mill (pitch 1), one `Hole { xy: (0,0), radius: 5.0, floor_z: 10.2 }`, `SrcRef::Entity("part")`: blocking warnings `Gouge { at: 4..=55 }` plus `Crossing { moves: [3, 56] } ...`.

**Likely cause.** The Thread kind verifies `Mode::Boundary` against the drill's rim region (`material_source::source_region`, Bore/Thread arm), and law (b) reads the declared rim at `r - tol`. A thread mill's helix runs the thread depth H (0.5413 x pitch) PAST the declared circle by design (`mill2d_c::thread_helices_are_timed_by_the_tools_pitch`: rho up to R + H - r), so every helix point reads as a gouge of about H against the rim. `mill2d_c` sources its threads from the stock, so it never sees this.

**What is owed.** Decide what a thread mill's rim is (the declared minor circle grown by the thread depth, or the major diameter) so a matched thread mill verifies clean against a model, while one cutting past the thread's major diameter still convicts; and look at the `Crossing` pairs on the same path.

**Done means:** a matched thread mill on a model-sourced hole verifies clean at full fidelity and near the refusal bound (`coarse_rims::a_thread_mill_reads_the_same_near_the_bound_as_at_full_fidelity` then tightens to `== Vec::new()`), and an oversize thread still convicts.

title: UI: native Open/Save dialogs can open behind the app window

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
## What

Every native picker (Open, Model, Save, Save As, Post, machine/post/theme picks) could
open **behind** the CamCraft window: the rfd dialog was created without an owner, and the
shell never asked for the foreground. A dialog opened right after launch — when the app was
started from a terminal or a script — was the worst case: the shell itself was not the
foreground window, so neither it nor its dialog was visible.

Reproduced on Windows 11 at 125 % scaling with the v0.18.0 release build: launch the app,
press Ctrl+O, and the `#32770` "Open" dialog exists but sits under the shell.

## Why

`crates/ui/src/file_dialog.rs` built `rfd::FileDialog` with title/filters/directory only —
`set_parent` was never called, so Windows had no owner to keep the dialog above. The shell
also never called `focus_window`, so a launch from a terminal left the app behind it, and an
owned dialog follows its owner's place in the z-order.

## Done means

- The shell asks for the foreground once, after the window is created.
- Every native picker is owned by the shell window, and the owner is raised just before the
  dialog opens.
- The GPU refusal `MessageDialog` is owned too.
- Hand-checked: launch from a terminal, first Ctrl+O, the dialog is visible in front; repeat
  for Save and Model.

Native dialog ownership has no headless test: rfd modals are hand-test-only in this repo
(`egui_app/tests.rs` says so), so the evidence is the hand check plus the z-order probe.

title: A matched drill is falsely convicted of a gouge on a reduced-fidelity model flagged above ~0.0105 mm

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while working #904 (pinning the containment solid law on a reduced-fidelity model). This is in the code PR #911 merged; #904's slice does not change it.

**What happens.** A drill matched to its hole, on a model flagged between about 0.0105 mm and 0.015 mm (the refusal bound), is convicted with `Gouge` at its first plunge, even when it stops well above the hole's floor. The gate then blocks the post with a gouge that is not there. Below about 0.0105 mm (a metre-unit file's 0.01 mm included) and at full fidelity it is clean.

**Repro.** A 40 x 40 x 20 block with a 20 x 20 blind hole to Z 10, a 4 mm drill (`DR-0400`), one `Hole { radius: 2.0, entry_z: 20.0, floor_z: 10.0 }`, Bottom Z 10.2:

| model imported at | blocking warnings |
|---|---|
| full fidelity, 0.008 ... 0.0105 mm | none |
| 0.011 mm, 0.012 mm, 0.0149 mm | `Gouge { at: 1 }` |
| 0.03 mm (refused by name at the gate) | none |

(`crates/app/tests/coarse_contain.rs` on #904's branch has the fixture; pass `Some(0.011)` and a bottom of 10.2.)

**Likely cause.** The section law (b) reads `floor = r - leave - cx.tightened(cx.gouge_tol)` (`sim` `verify/section.rs`). `GOUGE_TOL` exists to absorb the chord error of our own regions (`operation/material.rs`: "half the geo2d round-join chord error plus room for float chains"). A drill's region is the hole's rim as a polygon, so a matched drill's centre stands a few microns inside `r` by construction. Once the model's excess has taken more than about half the tolerance, what is left no longer covers that polygon's own sagitta, and the law convicts the drill against its own rim. The same may hold for other kinds whose regions carry our own chords (bore, thread mill, circular).

**What is owed.** Decide how law (b) should split its tolerance between our own discretization and the model's excess (for example: tighten only the part of the tolerance not spent on the region's own chord error, or build these rims finer), so an honest drill is not convicted on a model that is still judged.

**Done means:** a matched drill, bore and thread mill on a model flagged anywhere below the refusal bound verify clean, with a pin at 0.0149 mm; a real gouge there is still convicted.

body:
Part of #904. Found while working #904: swarf is the one multi-axis family still refused on a reduced-fidelity model.

**What is owed.** A swarf tool cuts with its flank. That the flank stands clear of the wall is proved only inside the generator (`motion` `multiaxis/stamp_pose.rs` and `stamp_rise.rs`, through `stamp_link::flank_clear` at the plan tolerance). No verify law re-measures it: law (f) judges the ball, and the reach laws judge the bands above the flute. So on a model imported coarser than promised there is no verdict to tighten, and `operation::fidelity_law::excess_aware` keeps Swarf and Advanced Swarf refused at the program gate.

Two ways to close it, to be decided by whoever takes it:

1. Thread the model's excess into the flank proof (`Ruled::tol` as `flank_clear` reads it), so the generator proves clearance with the tightened tolerance. This changes the paths generated on a reduced-fidelity model.
2. Add a verify law that measures the flank against the part, and tighten that. Larger, but it would also judge the flank at full fidelity, where today only the generator speaks.

**Done means:** Swarf and Advanced Swarf on a reduced-fidelity model are judged while a positive tolerance is left (and refused by name past that), with a pin for a flank cut between the tightened and the plain tolerance; or the refusal stays with the reason recorded in `docs/decisions`.

body:
Found while working #982. Part of #882 (its knife edge 3, "Rotary travel pins", which was not filed).

**What happens.** With the microlift acceptance settled (#982), the rotary Adaptive pins still turn on nanometres through the #850 planning budget. On unchanged upstream/main 3e9b8ae1 (release, Linux x86-64), with only `rings::open` eroding N nm deeper than it dilates back:

| fixture | level | 0 nm | 16 nm | 250 nm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r7 bar (`adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws`) | 5.0 | refused past the budget (85-86 revolutions), rings | refused, rings | **the budget passes it: HSM-planned, 5 in-cut breaks of 5.0-6.2 deg - the pin is red** (on main and with #982's fix alike) |
| r7 bar | 5.5 | HSM, lifted | HSM, lifted | main: rings (refused for travel - the lift edge #982 fixes); with #982: HSM, lifted |
| window (`the_developed_window_reaches_the_planner_and_names_each_refusal`) | 6.0, 5.0 | refused past the budget after 86 revolutions | refused after 85 | **the budget passes them**: main refuses them for travel (the lift edge); with #982 they are HSM-planned at 18.8 % D, 0 breaks |

So `adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws` is green on main only because the budget refuses level 5.0 at this exact geometry; a 250 nm change of the rings lets it through, it is planned, and the pin fails on the kink law (the breaks themselves are #1050).

**Why it matters.** Same as #982: a plan choice that flips on a nanometre-scale input blocks #882 and any other change to the planner's geometry, and a pin that is green by coincidence proves nothing.

**What #982 does and does not do.** It removes the lift-acceptance edge (the r6.2 neck levels 5.7 / 5.2 are HSM-planned at every perturbation tried). It does not touch `budget.rs` or `grow.rs` (PR #953 owns the latter).

Done means: the budget's verdict on the rotary window's and the r7 bar's levels is the same under a 16 nm - 0.25 um perturbation of the openings, pinned by perturbed twins the way #982 pins the slot; whichever way level 5.0 of the r7 bar is decided, its pin states it.

body:
Found while working #982 (branch `issue/982-microlift-acceptance`; decision record `docs/decisions/982-microlift-acceptance.md`).

**What happens.** When a developed neck band of `rotary_adaptive`'s bars is HSM-planned (kept in cut by microlift returns), two readings on the suite's 0.1 mm dexel stand past the laws the whole r7 bar is pinned to:

1. **Bore exit load.** The r6.2 bar's levels 5.7 and 5.2 both read **20.3 % D** (55.5 deg) at one move, the first turn out of the entry's bore (developed (21.7, 7.7) -> (20.8, 6.8) on 5.7). The law for the r7 bar is optimal + 35 % = 19.8 %. The planner's own 0.05 mm stock reads 47.5 deg there and names no overload; the r7 bar's lifted level 5.5 reads 53.0 deg (18.4 %) at the same place.
2. **In-cut breaks at the band's west end.** Level 5.2 of the r6.2 bar posts 3 breaks of 5.1, 5.5 and 5.5 deg near developed (-15.9, 4.7); level 5.0 of the r7 bar, when it is planned (see the budget knife edge, #1051), posts 5 breaks of 5.0-6.2 deg near (-18.3, 5.5). They are on the spiral's own chords (a piece cut on longer chords hides them some of the time).

**Why it was not seen.** Until #982 these bands were refused for travel on most runs (the microlift acceptance flipped on a sliver), so the plans were rarely posted and never pinned. #982's PR pins the r6.2 levels at what they read (`R62_LOAD_FACTOR` 1.40, `R62_BREAKS` 3 in `crates/motion/tests/rotary_adaptive.rs`) and names this issue.

**What they replace.** Offset rings on the same bands: 100 % D and 15-21 breaks of 45-135 deg. So this is owed polish, not a regression.

Done means: the r6.2 neck levels hold the whole bar's laws (dexel load <= optimal + 35 %, no in-cut break past 5 deg), `R62_LOAD_FACTOR` and `R62_BREAKS` are gone from the pin, and the r7 bar's level 5.0 holds them when it is planned.

PR #1032 (`Fixes #980`) found why two levels of the user's STEP bore fell back from the HSM plan to Offset rings: the entry orbit closed about 1e-15 mm off its own start, and the self-crossing check (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/guard.rs`) - which only skips NEIGHBOURING chords of one walk and tests exact signs - read the spiral leaving that point as crossing the orbit's first chord. The fix closes the orbit exactly (`rings.rs`, `circle`); the check itself is unchanged, on purpose.

Left open (high-tier review of #1032, https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1032#pullrequestreview-5868873098): the check stays exact-sign, so any other pair of walks that share a point to within rounding (a spiral that returns to its seed, a microlift return landing on a chord end, a ring that starts on the previous one) can still be reported as "crosses itself" and send a good level to Offset rings by name. Safe, but a silent loss of the adaptive plan the user asked for.

Expected: a shared end point (two chords touching at a common vertex within a stated tolerance far below the cutting tolerance) is not a crossing; a real crossing still is (the figure-eight unit test must stay green). State the tolerance and why it cannot hide a real self-cut. Related: #982 (microlift acceptance is a knife edge), #1010 (plans differ across platforms) - all three are about exact float comparisons in the planner.

Done means: a `crates/motion` test with two walks that touch at a shared point 1e-12 mm apart is not reported as crossing; the figure-eight still is; the heavy pins do not move, or the move is explained.

body:
Part of #361. Related: #864 (reduced-fidelity models), #904 (laws on a reduced-fidelity part).

**What happens.** A STEP that can only be meshed coarser than the importer promises (over the facet budget) is refused as a tool body by name (`tool_body_file::accept`): the collision laws read a body's envelope with no allowance for its chord error, and a coarse holder reads smaller than the holder is. That is safe, but vendor assemblies are often detailed (threads, lettering, small fillets), and the user's only way forward is to simplify the model elsewhere.

**Fix.** Take the body with its achieved chord error and judge it larger by that much: grow the spindle body's envelope bands (`HolderProfile`) radially and at both ends, and the lathe body's clearance spans (`LatheClearance`) on every side, by the excess over the importer's promise. Carry the chord on the body (project file too) and show it in the editor ("judged 0.04 mm larger"). Keep the refusal past a stated cap.

**Done means:** a body imported over budget lands, its judged envelope is never smaller than the full-fidelity one's (pinned by comparing the two on a curved fixture forced over budget), and a collision the full-fidelity body convicts is still convicted.

Part of #361.

**What happens.** A tool carries one body from one file. Modular tooling is sold and modelled in pieces: a clamping unit or basic holder on the turret or spindle, an adapter, a cutting head, the insert - joined at standardised interfaces (the issue names ISO 26622 and ISO 26623 polygon/taper couplings). Vendors publish one STEP per piece, so today the user must merge them in a CAD system before importing.

**Open design.** How a tool's body becomes a stack of placed pieces (each a file with its own placement relative to the one below), how the pieces mate (by the coordinate systems the files name, or by numbers), what the laws read (the union: one envelope for a spindle body, one set of clearance bands for a lathe body), and how it is saved. Only public documentation of the interface standards may be used; no vendor file is committed.

**Done means:** two synthetic pieces (our own STEPs) are attached to one tool, placed against each other, judged as one body, saved and reloaded; removing one piece is one undo step.

body:
Part of #361. Found while making lathe holder bodies reachable from the tool editor and MCP.

**What happens.** A turning tool can carry a lathe holder body (#369), and every move is judged against the part and the standing stock (`operation/turning_holder.rs`: "What stands. The part, always, and the stock less every cut"). The setup's workholding and fixtures are not in that reading. For a turning operation the fixture laws (`workholding_warnings` in `operation/generate.rs`) still sweep the tool record's holder cylinder (`tool_body::judged` returns the record unchanged for a lathe-frame body), and a turning insert's holder cylinder is normally 0 x 0. So an offset holder that runs into the chuck jaws, a tailstock or a steady rest passes with no finding - while the operation no longer carries the "holder not judged" note, because a body is present.

**Why it matters.** A user who imported the vendor's holder model reads "judged" as "judged against everything". A holder striking the chuck is a crash.

**Fix.** Read the lathe body's clearance bands (`camcraft_tools::lathe_holder::LatheClearance`) against the setup's steel as well: workholding that turns with the part as its revolved envelope (same reading as the stock), standing steel (tailstock, steady rest) in the machine frame. Until a kind of steel can be read, say so by name on the operation (a note like the existing "holder not judged"), never silently.

**Done means:** an offset lathe holder that reaches a chuck-jaw fixture is a blocking finding naming the move; the same holder clear of it passes; steel the law cannot read is named in a note. Pinned at the app level.

From the review of PR #990 (#891), non-blocking note: constant surface speed (G96) is clamped by the lower of the machine's `spindle_max` and the tool's `max_rpm`. There is no workholding limit: a chuck or collet has its own rated maximum rpm (often far below the spindle's), and the only place to state it today is the tool's `max_rpm`, which is the wrong owner (the same tool in a different chuck has a different limit).

**Why it matters:** under G96 the rpm rises as the diameter shrinks, so a facing pass toward the centre runs up to the clamp. A clamp above the chuck's rating is a safety hazard (jaws lose grip force at speed).

**Expected:** a setup on a lathe can state its workholding's maximum rpm. The G96 clamp (Fanuc `G50 S`, Tormach `G96 D`) and the G97 rpm check use min(machine, tool, workholding). An rpm above the workholding limit is refused by name, never silently capped. Undoable command plus MCP tool; old projects load with none.

**Done means:** a setup with a 2000 rpm chuck limit posts `G50 S2000` / `G96 D2000` for a G96 op whose tool and machine allow more, and refuses a G97 op asking 2500 rpm by name; pinned in `lathe_post_css`; round-trip pinned.

Depends on PR #990 merging (stack on it while it is open).

title: M12.1: machining mesh - crafted records that provoke every solidcore-tess shortfall, and a proven deviation bound for spline faces

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Follow-up of #940 (machining mesh seam, PR stacked on #941).

What #940 delivers: `camcraft_kernel::machining_mesh` refuses by name every `PlanStats` shortfall that touches the guarantee (unmeshed, lenient, unsampled edge, a face or edge capped off its tolerance), pinned by `every_planner_shortfall_is_a_refusal_or_a_note` on SYNTHETIC `PlanStats` values; and a SAMPLED deviation (15 barycentric points a triangle), judged by the closed-form distance to the record's analytic surface where the face is analytic, else by the parametric distance |S(u,v) - T(u,v)|.

Owed:
1. **Real provocations.** No fixture under testdata/models makes the planner report any shortfall (checked at 0.005, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0002 and 0.0001 mm on Milling-test.step and sample_ap214.step). Build small crafted records (a pcurve off its edge, a free edge, a face whose grid must be thinned past `MAX_FACE_GRID`, an edge past 20 000 nodes) and pin that each reaches its named `MeshRefusal` through `machining_mesh`, not only through `judge_stats`.
2. **Spline and revolved faces.** They are judged only by the parametric distance, which over-reads on a non-uniform parameterisation (a few per cent on a rational circle) - a possible false refusal. Add a projection onto the plan surface (Newton from the sample's (u, v)) so they get a true distance, with a fixture that has such a face.
3. **Between the samples.** The deviation is a sampled maximum, a lower bound of the true one; solidcore-tess meshes right up to the tolerance (0.993 of it on Milling-test). Either a stated bound on the sag between samples, or a margin in the seam, so "within" is a guarantee.

What upstream solidcore-tess would need (for the maintainer to raise; not filed upstream): a cancellation hook in `plan`; a per-face measured sag in `PlanStats` for every face; a stated bound on the sag between the planner's sample points.

Everything stays inside `crates/kernel`. Part of #27. Gates #917.

Done means: each shortfall entry is pinned by a crafted record through `machining_mesh`; a non-analytic face is judged by a projected distance with a fixture; the decision file says what bounds the sag between samples.

body:
Follow-up to #871 (refusal ghost for part-way refusals). The #871 PR adopted the ghost where the moves are in hand and the frame is already mapped to world by `run_job`. The remaining part-way refusals each need a frame map or a merge first, so they were listed in `docs/decisions/871-refusal-ghost-rest.md` rather than swept:

- **finishing3d raster / rings / swarf** (`raster.rs` `parallel`, `rings_and_tail`, `swarf_multi`): Rotary contour and parallel run these on frame-LOCAL facets (`multiaxis/rotary.rs` calls of `finishing3d::waterline` / `swarf`). First add `.map_err(GenError::without_ghost)` (or a `to_world` map) at those rotary calls, then adopt `with_ghost_moves(b.moves())`.
- **Rotary links and posing** (`rotary_links.rs` `radial_relink`, `rotary.rs` `posed`): rotary-local frame. Needs `f.to_world` plus the tip offset.
- **Face under an area turn** (`generate.rs` `turn_path(face_over(..)?, -turn)`): the refusal's spot (already today) and any ghost are in the turned frame. Map the spot and ghost back through `turn_path(-turn)`.
- **Cross drill app-side laws** (`cross_spindle.rs` `rapids_clear`, `cross_holder` on the spindle-shifted `t`): carry the ghost by the same shift `in_world` uses.
- **Nested refusals** (`machining3d/entry.rs` `pocket3d_air_split` material leg, `run_rest` rest ladder; `generate.rs` stitched contour runs): the inner refusal already carries its own ghost and `with_ghost` keeps it. Prepend the outer moves to it, which needs a small `Ghost` merge.
- **Multiaxis stamp / swarf link / curve walk, the rotary gate, the fixture route**: these are one-liners, but each needs its frame checked (posed or unposed world).

Done means: each site above either hands back its partial path in world coordinates (pinned by a test that its ghost lands where the part is) or is listed in a decision file with the reason. No generator's successful output changes, so goldens stay byte-identical.

Effort is `high` because it touches generator code (safety floor), even though the change is display-only.

Part of #261 (follow-up to #871).

The tool leaves the hole at the cycle's initial level (= R, the positioning rapid stands there) and the next motion is the home move. The committed golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/axial_drill.nc` (from `lathe_post.rs`, clearance 30, R 20) shows it:

```
G00 X0 Z20
G83 Z10 Q12000 F0.008
G80
M9
M05
G28 U0 W0        <- from Z20 (R); the verified path first rises to Z30
```

A lathe drills a single on-axis hole, so there is no traverse between holes. But the exit is lower than the verified motion, and `G28 U0 W0` moves X and Z together from there.

**Done means:** the lathe posts leave a face-drilling cycle at the stream's exit level. #994's law fits here too: the first rapid that leaves the hole ends the group (`G80`) and posts as the stream says. title: Adaptive plans differ across platforms on the same commit (likely libm last-place rounding)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found while working #984.

**What happens:** the same commit plans the same part differently on two platforms. `app pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (release) on ecb54b7f:

| platform | rings levels | moves / planar / arcs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows (the #850 measure, PR #865) | Z 20.000 | 5530 / 5497 / 600 |
| macOS, Apple silicon (Homebrew rustc 1.99.1) | Z 20.000 (crossing at -2.33, -2.78) | 5786 / 5753 / 651 |

macOS is deterministic run to run, so it is not hash-map order. Rust does not contract `a*b+c` into FMA unless asked, so the most likely cause is the platform libm: `f64::sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `hypot`, `exp`, `powf` call the system math library (MSVC CRT, glibc, Apple libm), which are not correctly rounded and differ in the last place. The STEP tessellation and the adaptive planner both use them, and the planner's crossing and acceptance tests are knife edges a 16 nm change flips (#882, #982). Not yet confirmed which call sites diverge, and not run on Linux.

**Why it matters:** a toolpath (and so the posted G-code) for the same part, tool and parameters depends on the OS the user runs. Every output is still verified and a crossing plan is refused by name, so this is not a gouge; but golden counts and exact plan pins cannot hold across platforms, and a user can see a different path from the same project file on two machines.

**Possible directions (open):** route the geometry and planner transcendental calls through a pure-Rust deterministic libm (the `libm` crate is already in Cargo.lock) so every platform rounds the same; or make the planner's decisions robust to sub-micron perturbation (#882, #982). Either changes toolpaths and needs every adaptive fixture re-measured.

Done means: the cause is confirmed on a second platform (Windows or Linux run of the bore test, plus which calls diverge), and either the output is made platform-identical with goldens re-measured, or the decision not to is recorded.

Refs #984, #882, #982.

body:
Found while writing the #926 per-post script suites.

**What is wrong.** `post --machine <file.mch>` (the command-line post, `crates/post/src/bin/post.rs`) hands the script `post::machine::script_props` of the raw file. `script_props` reads the static grammar (`kinematics.static.rotaries`, `kinematics.static.head.spindle.max`, `...toolStation.coolants`, `rapidRate`, ...). Every shipped machine in `assets/machines/` is a vendor kinematics tree (`kinematics.default.parts`), which the app first parses (`machine::parse_mch`) and then mirrors (`post::machine::mirror`) into that grammar. The binary parses the file only for its inverted-axis refusal and then drops the parsed machine, so the script sees no rotaries, no spindle limit, no coolant list, no rates.

Seen: `post --machine assets/machines/tilthead.mch fanuc.cps <tilted stream>` refuses "tilted move on a machine without a tilting rotary" although the file states A and B; posting the same stream with `mirror(parse_mch(..))` works (the #926 suites do that as a workaround, see `crates/post/tests/recorded/mod.rs`).

Why P1: the CLI posts a different program for the same machine than the app does (missing spindle cap, coolant codes and rotaries; refusals where the app posts).

Done means: the binary posts with the mirrored machine (keeping the raw file for `invert::apply`), so `post --machine <vendor .mch>` gives the app's program; pinned by a CLI test on `tilthead.mch`; the #926 runner then passes the file straight through.

title: Thread milling: refuse a hole the program has not drilled yet (the mill is not centre-cutting)

labels.name: bug

labels.name: P1

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Part of #894.

A thread mill is not centre-cutting, and the thread-milling ride (`machining2d::thread_ride`) feeds it down the hole's axis before the first lead-in arc. That is air only if an earlier operation opened the hole. Nothing checks it: the `Thread` operation generates and verifies clean on a part whose hole is modelled, even when the program holds no drilling operation before it and the stock at the hole is solid. The gouge laws read the part (the hole is in the model), so they see nothing; the centre-cutting audit (`operation::plunge_solid`, `camcraft_motion::plunge_law`) is not asked for this kind, and it reads the raw stock, which would refuse every thread.

**Effect:** forget the tap drill and the program plunges a thread mill into solid metal at plunge feed - a broken cutter, with no finding at generate, at verify or at the post gate.

**Fix sketch:** read the stock the setup's earlier operations leave standing (the prior grid the drilling laws already read, `operation::drill_prior`) under each threaded hole: the tool's full cylinder down the axis and the first pass's lead-in must fall through air. Refuse by name at generate ("the hole at (x, y) is not drilled yet - add a drilling operation before the thread") and digest the program ahead in the stamp, so reordering the operations marks the thread Stale.

**Done means:** a Thread operation with no drilled hole under it is refused by name; the same operation after a Drill of at least the tool's diameter generates; moving the Drill after the Thread turns it Stale and refuses; pinned by an app test. The milled `Bore` ride's axis entry gets the same reading or its own issue.

body:
Part of #894.

The `Thread` operation cuts only the 60-degree ISO metric / unified form: `camcraft_tools::thread_mill::form_refusal` refuses a thread mill ground to any other angle by name, and the depth is the ISO 724 constant `0.5413 x pitch`.

**What is missing**
- 55-degree Whitworth (BSW / BSP parallel): its own depth law (0.6403 x pitch, rounded crests and roots).

- Trapezoidal and ACME forms (30 / 29 degrees).
- Pitch entry in threads per inch for unified threads.

Each form needs its depth law from the public standard (BS 84, ASME B1.20.1, ISO 2904, ASME B1.5), the form door widened to it, and the root / crest gouge readings (`operation::thread_op`) taking that depth.

**Done means:** a thread mill of each supported form threads a modelled hole of that standard, verifies clean and posts; a form with no depth law is still refused by name; pinned by goldens.

title: Adaptive microlift acceptance is a knife edge: lift_returns compares equal half-degree readings, so a 16 nm geometry change flips the slot's plan

labels.name: bug

labels.name: effort:max

body:
Found while working #882 (held branch `issue/882-adaptive-open-simplify` @ 70ac996f; see https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/882#issuecomment-6811353217).

**What happens:** `adaptive/lift.rs` `lift_returns` keeps the microlifted plan only when its worst reading is not above the spiral's, and both are read in half-degree steps. On main, the 60 x 14 slot reads 48.0 against 48.0. Any geometry perturbation, even a 16 nm thinning of the opening, makes the spiral read 47.5, so the lifted plan is dropped and the slot falls from HSM (15.7 % load) to Offset rings.

**Why it matters:** a plan choice that flips on a nanometre-scale input is a knife edge. It blocks #882's speedup (the bore goes from 115.6 s to 2.2 s) and any other change that perturbs the planner's geometry.

Done means: the acceptance compares within a stated tolerance, not on equal half-degree steps. A pinning test shows the slot keeps the same plan under a perturbation of the opening's area in the 16 nm to 0.25 um range, and no adaptive fixture's verdict changes on main.

Part of #882.

Found while working #885.

**What happens:** `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps` on a 4th axis without TCP (`machine.rtcp` false - e.g. an A that states no tilting direction) resets its modal angle memory `lastA = 0` at every tool change (`onToolChange`) and starts the program at `lastA = 0`. A tilted record at A0 then writes no A word, although the post never commanded A0 and the table may stand anywhere. Reproduced on main (f490458a) with `rotaryBrake: true`:

```
TOOL 1 T1 / SECTION / Rapid ... A 30000 / Feed ... A 30000 / ENDSECTION
TOOL 2 T2 / SECTION / Rapid ... A 0     / Feed ... A 0     / ENDSECTION
```

posts `G00 X0 Y0 Z5 A30` for the first tool, then for the second tool `G00 X0 Y0 Z5` and `G01 X0 Y0 Z0 F100` with no `A0` - the second operation cuts at A30.

**Expected:** the first A of a program, and the first A after anything that may have moved the table, is written; the modal memory is the angle the post last wrote, never an assumed 0. (The G43.4 branch is not affected - its arm writes all three words.)

PR for #885 reads the held angle only from the A words a block actually wrote, so a non-TCP feed that turns from an A the post never placed is now refused by name when the A states a rate - but with no stated rate the wrong program above still posts.

Done means: a pinning test posting the two-tool stream above writes A0 for the second tool (and an opening A0), goldens moved only where an A word was missing, each listed.

title: M12.1: a machining mesh from solidcore-tess - largest mesh-to-surface deviation benched, and every planner shortfall a refusal

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: area:3d

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What is left of point 4 of #916 (tessellation), found while benching it.

Facts from the bench (`crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`, solidcore pin `55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda`): solidcore now has a mesher, `solidcore-tess`, which meshes the STEP reader's B-rep record at a chord tolerance in millimetres. At the app's 0.005 mm cap it is watertight on every fixture when vertices are welded by exact position (truck's per-face meshes leave 854 open triangle sides on Milling-test.step and 3196 on sample_ap214.step by the same count), and its volume and area are closer to the exact solid than truck's (5.6e-5 against 1.2e-4 relative on Milling-test). It uses more triangles (6228 against 952).

Owed before #917 can make the app's mesh with it:

1. **The deviation that matters for a gouge check is not measured yet.** The bench compares volume, area, bounding box and watertightness. It does not measure the largest distance from the mesh to the exact surface. Bench it per fixture against the chord asked for (0.005 mm, and the caps of #689 / #864), for solidcore-tess and for truck's mesh, and pin the verdicts.
2. **Its own docs call it a display mesher** ("a display mesh decides nothing a model depends on: it is drawn, never measured"), and it reports what it could not do in `PlanStats` instead of failing: `unmeshed`, `lenient` (a face filled leniently so the display has no hole), `over_tolerance`, `edges_capped`, `unsampled_edges`. A machining import must turn every one of those into a named refusal or a reduced-fidelity flag (#864 / PR #911), never a silent mesh. Decide which, per entry, and pin each with a fixture that provokes it.
3. **Triangle budget.** The app caps facets (`MAX_FACETS`) and coarsens to stay inside memory. solidcore-tess has its own bounds; state how the app's budget maps onto them.
4. **wasm32.** `solidcore-tess` gates rayon off on wasm32 in its manifest; a wasm32 check of it has not been run from this workspace.

Everything stays inside `crates/kernel` until #917 (low coupling, #919).

Part of #27. Gates #917.

Done means: the deviation bench runs in the kernel's lane with its table pinned; each `PlanStats` shortfall has a decided outcome and a test; the answer on the triangle budget and on wasm32 is a comment here.

title: M12.1: solidcore's tight bounding box takes the whole cylinder of a trimmed face (Milling-test.step: Y max 30.0, true 19.719), plus two smaller findings at pin 55d0e763

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: blocked
labels.description: Waiting on another issue or a decision

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Found by the STEP bench of #916 (`crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`), at the solidcore pin `55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda`.

**1. Wrong bounding box (the one that matters).**
`testdata/models/Milling-test.step` (and its inch twin) is a 60 mm disc with a flat at Y = 19.719. Imported through `camcraft_kernel::solidcore_step`, the solid's volume (52808.744 mm^3) and area (11143.378 mm^2) agree with truck's mesh to 1.2e-4, but `StepSolid::measure`'s box - the port's `calculate_bounding_box` with `tight: true` - is `[-30, -30, -5]..[30, 30, 20]`. The file's own vertices, truck's mesh and solidcore's own mesh (`solidcore-tess`) all stop at Y = 19.719. The box takes the whole R = 30 cylinder, not the trimmed face. It is pinned in the bench as `disagree: bounding box`.

Not known yet: whether the port's box is wrong for any trimmed periodic face, or whether the record-to-kernel build (`solidcore_convert::brep::to_kernel_body`) gives the face a parameter box that covers the whole circle. A kernel-made fixture (a cylinder cut by a plane through the seam's own booleans) would tell the two apart.

Why P1: stage 5 (#917) puts imported geometry under every toolpath. A box 10 mm too large would mis-size automatic stock and mis-place anything aligned to the part's extent.

**2. Stale cached topology after the build.** `to_kernel_body` hands out a B-rep whose cached `Face::shell` is behind its face-use links on every fixture; the port's `topology::integrity::check` refuses it ("cached face shell: face 0 not found"). The seam works around it with `Brep::refresh_cached_topology()` (public; rewrites the cached fields only). To report upstream (tangency-labs/solidcore); the maintainer decides who files it there.

**3. No cancellation in the STEP topology pass.** `solidcore_step::topology::read_solids` takes no progress or cancel hook, so the importer's time bound cannot stop it; it is bounded only by the reader's caps and the seam's 64 MiB size bound. To raise upstream, or to bound by calling the per-solid readers from the seam.

Part of #27. Gates #917.

Done means: the Milling-test rows of the bench read `agree` (the box fixed at its source, or the importer taking its box from a source that is right, with the reason recorded), the root cause is named in a decision entry, and findings 2 and 3 are either fixed at a new pin or filed upstream with their links here.

body:
What happens: the reach laws decide "upright" with an exact float compare (`is_vertical` in `crates/sim/src/verify/`). A move whose axis is off vertical by rounding noise (about 1e-10 degrees, as a rotated setup or a posed operation can produce) takes the tilted-tool path, and a holder wider than the cutter then flips to a collision the upright path would not report. Found by the high-tier re-review of PR #843 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/843#pullrequestreview-5866435965, "older bug, not from this PR"). For the shanks #843 newly checks the reviewer measured no such flip up to about 0.015 degrees.

Why it matters: not a silent pass - a false collision that blocks a good program, and one that appears or disappears with floating-point noise.

Expected: "upright" is decided with a stated angular tolerance, and a tilt inside it is judged exactly as a vertical move; a real small tilt (above the tolerance) is judged as tilted. The tolerance and why it is safe (how far a band can move sideways at that angle over the tool's length, against the gouge tolerance) go in `docs/decisions/`.

Also from the same review, smaller: a tilted tool with both its shank and its holder in the part reports the same `ShankHit` twice for one move - de-duplicate per move and group.

Done means: a test with a holder wider than the cutter gets the same verdict at 0 and at 1e-10 degrees of tilt, and a tilted verdict at a real small tilt; the duplicate hit is gone; no existing verdict or golden changes. Tests live in `crates/sim/tests` where no app fixture is needed.

title: MCP: set WCS from feature picks

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
PR #706 grew the GUI's "Set WCS from features": pick edges, vertices, faces and cylinder walls, say which axis each one sets, and the WCS lands on the fitted frame, undoable (#701). The MCP surface cannot do the equivalent. `set_wcs` (`crates/app/src/mcp/setup_tools.rs`) takes only an absolute origin or a stock-bbox point plus offset, and rotation is a raw unit quaternion - so an agent has to solve the frame maths itself from `list_features` output, and a wrong quaternion posts shifted toolpaths with no diagnostic.

The id-driven precedent already exists: `locate_part` mates part/fixture features **by `list_features` id** and fits the 3-2-1 itself; `set_operation_geometry` takes the same ids.

**Proposal:** a tool (say `set_wcs_from_features`) taking the active setup and picks as `[{id, role}]` with `role` in `origin | x | y | z`, and:

- runs the GUI's exact law - `pick::roles::align_roles` (`crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs`): Z, X, Y priority, first axis exact, second projected perpendicular, third derived to close the frame; origin anchored at the feature's natural centre; cylinder walls by covariance fit. No second frame law to drift;
- returns refusals as MCP error strings, the same named ones the GUI says: too few picks, duplicate role, fewer than two axes, parallel axes (5 degree tilt rule), zero-length edge, unresolvable datum, stale feature id;
- queues the existing `CommandKind::SetWcs` - no new command kind, one undoable step. The "commands ship with an MCP tool" rule is satisfied by the tool itself (as noted on #706).

Filed at the reviewer's suggestion in the #706 review (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/706): keep the agent surface level with the GUI. Related: #701, #709.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P0

labels.name: area:post

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What happens: a setup on work offset 5 or 6 posts through `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps` with the word `G58` / `G59` written verbatim in each section's opening block. The script's own notes say otherwise for this control: its comment near line 484 calls G58 / G59 "axial programmable offsets", `frameOf` (line 536) maps the settable frames as `G54..G57 -> 1..4, G505..G599 -> 5..99`, and its probing refusal says "only the settable frames G54..G57 / G505..G599 can be set on this control". So on an 840D the fifth and sixth settable frames are `G505` and `G506`; `G58` / `G59` do not select a work offset - the program would run in the wrong frame or alarm.

Found while detailing #931 (2026-11-11). No golden covers offsets 5 or 6 on this post.

To do: confirm against Siemens' public programming documentation (settable zero offsets G54-G57, G505-G599; G58 / G59 axial programmable offset on the 840D sl), then either write `G505` / `G506` for offsets 5 and 6, or refuse those offsets by name on this post - record the choice in `docs/decisions/`. One source of truth: the work offset still comes only from the setup (`setup::wcs_slot`); only the word this post writes changes.

Related: #931 (work offsets as an index, the post supplies the word) would make this mapping the post's job by design; this issue is the wrong output today and does not wait for it.

Done means: a pinning test posts setups on offsets 1-6 through the Sinumerik post and asserts the word for each (or the named refusal); the test lives with the post suites (#926 when it exists); no other post's goldens change.

title: Work offsets: core uses an index, the post supplies the word and display name

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
## Problem

A setup stores its work offset as an index (`SetupDef::work_offset`), but core
turns that index into a Fanuc-style word before any post is involved:

- The table `WCS_SLOTS = ["G54".."G59"]` lives in `camcraft-app`
  (`operation/types/sel.rs`) and is read directly by the Setups page combo,
  `setup::wcs_label`, the setup sheet, the MCP `set_work_offset` tool and the
  refusal messages.
- `posting::wcs_context` writes the word, not the index, into the stream as
  `PARAM WorkOffset`. Posts then parse it back: Fanuc and Mazak use
  `slotOf("G55") -> 1`, Heidenhain regex-matches `^G5([4-9])$` to pick a preset
  row.
- An index of 6 or more is refused in core, so extended offsets
  (`G54.1 P..`, Sinumerik `G505+`, further Heidenhain preset rows) cannot be
  expressed.

A setup with no machine and no post still shows `G54`: the word comes from
neither. Every other ask in the stream is already dialect-neutral (coolant,
after-operation); the work offset is the exception.

## Proposal

1. **Stream carries the index.** `PARAM WorkOffset` becomes a 1-based number.
   A manifest flag (`workOffsetIndex = true`) opts a script in, following the
   `coolantModes` / `afterModes` pattern. A script without the flag keeps
   receiving the word for offsets 1-6, so user-loaded posts keep working, and
   is refused by setup name for any offset above 6.
2. **Each post maps the index to its own word** and refuses, by setup name,
   an index it cannot express. The limit becomes the post's, not core's.
3. **The post supplies the display name.** A script may define a function
   (for example `workOffsetName(n)`) returning what the control calls offset
   `n` ("G55", "G54.1 P3", "preset 2"). The UI, setup sheet, MCP tool and
   refusal messages show "WCS n (name)" for the setup's resolved post.
4. **Fallback.** A script that defines no name function shows plain "WCS n".
5. **Core and UI speak indexes.** `WCS_SLOTS` leaves `camcraft-app` and
   `camcraft-ui`, apart from the two pre-v54 file migrations that need the old
   words to read old files.

## Out of scope

- The project file format: it already stores the index, so no version step.
- The legacy `G54` entity name of a document without setups (internal name
  only; renaming it would need a migration for no user benefit).
- Rotated work offsets (#315, #760).

## Open questions

- Where the name lookup lives so the layering holds (ui -> app -> post): an
  app-level function that evaluates the setup's post, with caching, since the
  UI must not evaluate scripts per frame.
- The MCP tool's input: accept an index, and keep accepting the old words as
  aliases for 1-6?
- Whether the six-offset cap is replaced by a per-post maximum the script
  declares, so the combo can list the right number of entries.
- Whether the simulator or any test harness parses the posted offset word
  back; not yet checked.

## Acceptance

- Every existing posted-program golden is byte-identical (the 148 that
  contain a `G5x` word included).
- Every shipped `.cps` declares the flag and maps the index itself; no
  `slotOf`-style parsing of a word remains.
- A setup can be given offset 7 or higher and posts correctly on a dialect
  that supports it; a dialect that does not refuses by setup name.
- A user post without the flag posts offsets 1-6 exactly as before.
- The Setups page shows the resolved post's name for each offset, and
  "WCS n" when the post supplies none.
- `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describe the new
  value, flag and name function.

## Related

Background (closed):

- #196 and #342 introduced the current design: G54-G59 is the setup's post
  label.
- #51 added Heidenhain preset selection for other work offsets - the source
  of the `G5x` -> preset-row regex.
- #876 already called "work offset word" jargon in the UI.

Open work this touches:

- #836 (TinyG post) and #728 (Sienci AltMill on the grblHAL post) add new
  `.cps` files that would need the flag and the mapping.
- #258 (Post dialog) touches the same post-options area.
- #760 (rotated work offset) touches the WCS code; rotation stays out of
  scope here.

title: Gate cost: a high-cohesion, low-coupling plan for crates and tests (umbrella - needs breakdown)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Maintainer direction (2026-11-11): "We should aim for a high cohesion low coupling thru out our codebase as we are built crates and tests. And every gate is very costly."

Where the cost comes from today (measured 2026-11-11 on main 0e36fd14):

| Crate | Source lines | Test files (one binary each) | Depends on (workspace) |
|---|---|---|---|
| app | 72,122 | 267 | cl, geometry, motion, post, sim, tools |
| ui | 57,060 | 14 | app |
| motion | 46,643 | 65 | cl, geometry, sim, tools |
| sim | 23,444 | 50 | cl, geometry, tools |
| post | 6,181 | 5 | cl, geometry |
| geometry | 5,539 | 4 | - |
| tools | 4,306 | 1 | - |
| cl | 3,723 | 1 | - |
| kernel | 1,185 | 5 | - |

- `app` is the hub: it depends on every domain crate, so almost any change rebuilds it, and each of its 267 test files links the whole crate into its own binary.
- Tests of one domain's behaviour live in `app` (post dialect tests such as `fanuc_post`, `tormach_post`, `heidenhain_*` sit in `crates/app/tests/` while `crates/post/tests/` has 5 files), so a post-only change still builds and links `app`.
- A geometry / cl / Cargo change falls back to the batch tier.
- Each worktree's `target/` is 25-56 GB; five builds at once took the disk from 166 GB to 13 GB free on 2026-11-11.

Open questions to answer here (research, no code):
1. Fan-out: for a change in each crate, which crates and how many test binaries rebuild and relink, and how long does it take (cold and warm, with #913's cache)? One table.
2. Test placement: which `crates/app/tests/*` files test behaviour owned by post, sim, motion, cl, tools or geometry and could move to that crate with a small fixture seam instead of the whole app? Count per target crate.
3. Test binaries: what does folding a crate's test files into a few binaries (one per gate-map group) save in link time and disk, and what does it cost (`gate test <name>` selection, parallel runs, the quick tier's changed-test picking in `xtask/src/plan.rs`)?
4. Coupling: which `app` modules could become their own crate (the M4.1 seams still inside `app`: operation, project, commands, mcp, machine), and which dependencies between domain crates could be cut or inverted (motion -> sim; the new post -> tools from PR #880)?
5. Rules: which of this becomes law in AGENTS.md "Code shape" and a reviewer check (e.g. a test lives in the crate that owns the behaviour; a new dependency between workspace crates needs a decision entry; no new test file in `app` for behaviour another crate owns)?

Then file the concrete sub-issues (each with P*, effort, area, "Done means", "Part of #<this>"), ordered by gate minutes saved per unit of work, and close this umbrella.

Related: #900 / PR #913 (compile cache and lighter dev profile), #27 (kernel seam).

body:
Maintainer decision (2026-11-11): "Solidcore do support STEP now ... We should replace truck with solidcore", and, asked how to depend on it: git pin, bench first. This supersedes "STEP IO stays on truck" in #27 and in `docs/decisions/27-solidcore-healing.md` (decision 4).

Facts (checked 2026-11-11):
- Upstream `tangency-labs/solidcore` has `crates/solidcore-step` (STEP read and write: Part 21 exchange structure, Part 42 geometry and topology, units), moved in from SolidCraft on 2026-11-10.
- It is `publish = false` and depends by path on the repo's `solidcore`, `solidcore-convert`, `solidcore-ops` and `solidcore-record`. Only `solidcore` 1.0.1 is on crates.io (what `crates/kernel` pins today). So this needs a git dependency on the solidcore workspace, kernel included.

This issue (first step, bench only - the app's import path does not change):
1. In `crates/kernel` only: depend on the solidcore workspace crates at ONE pinned upstream commit (`rev = "<full sha>"`, never a branch). Record the sha, what differs from 1.0.1 for the calls the seam already makes, and the licence texts (`assets/ui/LICENSES.md`) in `docs/decisions/`. The existing kernel suites (agreement bench, heal, corrupt-input corpus) must stay green on the pinned commit, or the differences are listed and decided.
2. A STEP importer on the solidcore side of the seam (`solidcore_step_import` or similar): file bytes -> solid(s) + units + diagnostics, with a size bound and a time bound like `import_smb`. Degenerate and corrupt input gives a named error, never a panic or hang.
3. A dual-importer agreement bench against truck-stepio over every STEP file under `testdata/models/` (and the fuzz / corrupt corpus): per file, both import, or one refuses by name; where both import: solid count, bounding box, volume and area agree within a stated tolerance, units agree (mm, inch, metre files - #306, #689), and the empty-parameter-list file of #887 imports. Verdicts pinned in a table like stages 1-3; a disagreement is recorded, never averaged away.
4. Tessellation: state how a solidcore-imported solid becomes the mesh CamCraft machines against (chord tolerance, the caps of #689 / #864), and bench mesh deviation against truck's on the same files. If solidcore has no tessellator fit for it, say so - that decides the second step's shape.
5. wasm32 still builds (`crates/kernel` is in #27's retirement gate).

Not in this issue: switching `crates/app`'s import to solidcore, removing truck or ruststep (next issue).

Clean-room note: solidcore is an Apache-2.0 port of NVIDIA's SMLib and solidcore-step is written from ISO 10303-21 / -42; no HSMWorks material is involved. Provenance comments say so.

Part of #27.

Done means: the bench runs in the kernel's lane with its verdict table pinned; the pinned sha and what it brings are in `docs/decisions/`; the report on tessellation and on any file where the two importers disagree is a comment here.
